newsitem.title: GERMANY: German chemical employers say pay deal reached. [CORRECTED 23:57 GMT]
newsitem.headline: German chemical employers say pay deal reached. [CORRECTED 23:57 GMT]

text.p: German chemical employers said on Wednesday they had reached a 1997 wage deal including a 1.5 (corrects from 1.6) percent rise in pay for workers in the west German chemical industry.
They said that the agreement reached with the IG Chemie trade union also maintained sick pay at the full 100 percent of salary, in return for which reductions are to be made to other worker bonuses.

Under the agreement, which applies to the some 590,000 workers in the west German chemical industry, the existing "thirteenth month" year-end bonus is to be reduced from 100 percent of a month's salary to 95 percent.

Part of the savings from the reduction of the year-end bonus can, on a voluntary basis within individual companies, be used on measures aimed at reducing absenteeism in the sector, employer and union negotiators said.
Employers also committed themselves to providing at least the same number of trainee positions open in the industry for 1997 as were available this year.
The agreement follows protests by chemical workers at plans by some companies to implement a new law cutting sick pay entitlements from 100 percent of salary to 80 percent.
